correctness.rationale: Cyclic symmetrization of any constant-preserving linear center functional is norm nonincreasing and equals the vertex mean. For the mean, triangle inequality gives the exact maximum of 1 and the average chord-power sum; a distance-to-vertex function attains the center component. The chord-product n gives F'(0)=log(n)/n>0 and F''>0, yielding unique phase crossing since (2/n)cot(pi/(2n))>1. The discrete squared log-chord mean converges by endpoint-dominated Riemann sums and Parseval to pi^2/12. Uniform third derivative bounds yield n(F(c/sqrt(n))-1)->-1+pi^2 c^2/24, and monotonicity squeezes the threshold. The explicit standalone verifier passed 751 supplementary checks; it is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This complete family-level threshold separates nonlinear norm-one extension of individual scalar functions from simultaneous real-linear norm-one extension. It resolves precisely how much snowflaking removes the linearity obstruction, including the sharp n^{-1/2} rate governed by logarithmic chord variance. This is a motivated geometric/operator invariant across arbitrarily many vertices, not an arbitrary finite table or a trivial renaming.
